note: THE LEG RECORD'S SHAPE, AND THE TEXT THE MODEL IS SHOWN BEFORE IT
COMPOSES ONE (kogaki#1108).
WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR, stated first because it is what separates it from
every other schema carrier in src/. The other schemas are read by a
validator and by nothing else: they describe a record the composing party
already knows the shape of. This one is read TWICE, and the second reader
is the point. `validateLegs` in src/compose.mjs reads the field set from
it, and the path-composition state of the Brief workflow table RENDERS it
into the judge's prompt. So the text the Model composes against and the
text the refusal enforces are one file and cannot disagree.
THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES, measured on 2026-09-12 over the two live Briefs
(theses/calling-saved-permission-durable-leaves and
theses/legs-real-quality-matter-degree). No file declared the Leg's
fields or what they mean. The composer inferred the shape from
.claude/skills/brief/SKILL.md's prose, wrote a Candidates JSON, and
`validateLegs` checked it afterwards -- so the only Harness text carrying
what a field means was a refusal string, seen only when shape had already
failed. Claim cardinality drifted accordingly: the first Brief carried 1
to 3 claims per Leg, the second 4 to 6, with up to six claims from one
Strand in a single Leg.
IT CARRIES THE RULES OVER THE WHOLE PATH TOO (kogaki#1147). The field
table below is about one Leg; `path_rules` is about the sequence -- the
Section grouping, the order `depends_on` may name, the uniqueness of an id,
the claim cardinality. Those were enforced in src/compose.mjs and stated
nowhere a composer reads, so a path satisfied them by chance or learned
them from a refusal that had already spent an attempt. The refusals now
read their text from that section, for the reason the field set is read
from this one.
IT DECLARES SHAPE AND MEANING, AND JUDGES NEITHER. Every MUST of the
composition design stays judgment-class and is judged at path review. A
missing field is refused here; a weak rationale is not, and no description
below is ever matched against a value.
SPEC REFERENCES IN THIS FILE (kogaki#902; one carrier, kogaki#982).
The rule these entries are written under -- what a copy is, what the two
markers `[implemented-against: ...]` and `[see: ...]` mean, and why nothing
names a section number or a line range -- lives in ONE place:
`src/SPEC-REFERENCES.md`. It is not restated here.

what_a_leg_is: A Leg is one stretch of the Reader Path: the Leg Waypoints that serve one
higher-order relation of the Brief's RelationalStructure, in order
(kogaki#1768, owner decision 2026-11-10). A Leg binds no Move: its Waypoints
are composed from the structure's relations, the Legs are derived over them
by the runner, and the paragraph Move is bound once, per Leg Waypoint, by
The Leg's shape is the field table below. Every field written for a Leg Move's
binding is retired and refused by name: `move`, `no_move_fits`, `materials`,

leg_id.description: This Leg's own id, unique within the path.

relation.description: The id of the higher-order relation of the Brief's `structure` this Leg serves, as the derivation's partition records it (kogaki#1768). Present on every Leg of a Brief that carries a `structure`, and refused on a Leg of a Brief that carries none.

reaches_target.description: Present, and true, on exactly ONE Leg of the path: the LAST, the Leg whose last Waypoint carries the apex (kogaki#1768). That Leg is the one that attains the Thesis: the Brief's Reader target heading renders the Thesis (kogaki#1699), and the Brief's derived Thesis row is handed to this Leg (kogaki#1328).

claims.description: What this Leg ASSERTS, one entry per Strand its Waypoints serve. A claim is a PROPOSITION ABOUT THE WORLD and names no reader. Its ground is the pinned Lesson, held as an address in the Brief's Strands section and never copied here. See `claim` below.

waypoints.description: The points this Leg's paragraphs make, as an ORDERED list of waypoints, composed from the Brief's RelationalStructure (kogaki#1768). Each waypoint is a POINT: the proposition its paragraph makes, in the article's subject, one sentence (kogaki#1326) -- what the paragraph establishes, never how the reader is to feel or what they are handed. Each names the claim or claims of this Leg it serves, and every claim of this Leg is served by at least one waypoint. One waypoint is one paragraph, and /paragraph-plan binds its Move. See `waypoint` below.

opens_section.description: Present on a Leg that opens a Section of the finished article, written by the `leg_sections` row (kogaki#1768). ITS VALUE STATES THE SECTION'S DESTINATION, not a title (owner decision 2026-10-10): one plain sentence or phrase stating where the Section's last claims leave the reader, in EVERYDAY WORDS, so a reader can skip directly to any Section and still understand its heading. The grouping rules are a property of the WHOLE PATH and run after every Leg is known to be well formed -- they are stated in `path_rules` below, as the validator checks them.

note: THE RULES OVER THE WHOLE PATH, AND WHY THEY ARE DECLARED HERE
(kogaki#1147). Everything above is a rule about ONE Leg, and a composer
was already shown it. The rules below are about the PATH -- a Leg's
relation to its neighbours, and the sequence taken as a whole -- and until
this issue they lived in code alone: `validateLegs` and
`sectionGroupingRefusal` in src/compose.mjs raised them, and the composing
party met one for the first time in a refusal that had already cost one of
its three attempts. Two runs on 2026-09-18 died at path composition on the
Section grouping's rule 4, each having satisfied every field-level rule it
was shown. A rule enforced over a record and never stated to the party
that composes it can be satisfied only by chance.
THE REFUSALS READ THEIR TEXT FROM THE ENTRIES BELOW, which is the same
arrangement the field table above already has: the prompt and the refusal
cannot disagree when there is one file. A rule stated here with no refusal
reading it, or a refusal composing its own wording, is the two-carrier
drift this file exists to remove -- and `checks/check-brief-compose.sh`
reads every refusal these two functions raise back against this section.
EACH ENTRY CARRIES `name` AND `rule`. The `name` is what the refusal says
first, so a refused composer can find the rule it broke by searching this
file for the words it was just handed; the `rule` is the rule as the
validator checks it. `class` is `checked` where a refusal enforces it and
`judgment` where it is yours to make -- a judgment-class rule is stated
HERE, beside the checked ones, because the two read alike to whoever
composes against them and only one of them will ever refuse. Nothing
below is matched against a value: a rule marked `judgment` is judged at
path review, and Every MUST is judgment, and nothing becomes a lint is the
rule that keeps it there.
The Section grouping is where the four Section rules are ratified; the
Leg's shape carries the path's own order and the uniqueness of an id; the
claims rule carries the cardinality.

path_is_non_empty.name: the Leg's shape -- a path is an ordered sequence of Legs
path_is_non_empty.rule: A composed path is a NON-EMPTY, ORDERED array of Leg records, read in the order it is written.

leg_id_unique.name: the Leg's shape -- one id per Leg
leg_id_unique.rule: Each `leg_id` is unique within the path.

one_claim_per_strand.name: the claims rule -- one claim per Strand, per Leg
one_claim_per_strand.rule: A Leg asserts ONE claim on behalf of each Strand its Waypoints serve. A Strand that serves several Legs carries its claim in each.

section_rule_1.name: the Section grouping rule 1
section_rule_1.rule: A Leg OPENS a Section when it changes the reader's question -- its Waypoints carry a higher-order relation the previous Leg did not. This is the positive case and it is the `leg_sections` row's TO JUDGE: nothing checks it.

section_rule_3.name: the Section grouping rule 3
section_rule_3.rule: The FIRST Leg of the path always opens a Section. A path that declares `opens_section` nowhere renders as one unbroken run of prose, which is the second of the two drafts the 2026-09-03 ruling rejected.

section_rule_4.name: the Section grouping rule 4
section_rule_4.rule: TWO ADJACENT SECTIONS HOLDING EXACTLY ONE LEG EACH are refused with a request to MERGE them, because a heading on every Leg is the first of the two drafts the ruling rejected. Length enters as a bound on the grouping, never as its reason.
section_rule_4.the_other_clause: Rule 4's other clause -- a Section running past roughly a display and a half of prose without a heading -- measures REALIZED PROSE, which no Brief contains. It is a named deferred slot in the Section grouping: it binds your judgment while you group the Legs, and no refusal reads it.

reaches_target_marked.name: the Reader target Leg -- exactly one Leg marked, and it is the last
reaches_target_marked.rule: EXACTLY ONE Leg of the path carries `reaches_target: true`, and it is the LAST Leg (kogaki#1768): the derived Legs end on the one whose last Waypoint carries the apex. Zero marked Legs leaves the Brief's Reader target undecided; two or more leaves it ambiguous which Leg attains the Thesis.

definition: A CLAIM IS THE ONE PROPOSITION THIS LEG ASSERTS ON BEHALF OF ONE
STRAND, FOR THIS READER AT THIS POINT IN THE PATH.
ITS GROUND IS THE PINNED LESSON, HELD AS AN ADDRESS AND NEVER COPIED.
In Toulmin's layout the claim is what is asserted and the ground is the
data it rests on; this field carries the assertion, and the Lesson it
rests on stays at its pin in the Brief's Strands section. The Lesson's
own Claim sentence is at that pin and is never rendered here or in the
Leg Packet, which is what keeps `assert nothing beyond` checkable:
what the Leg may assert is this list, and nothing arrives beside it.
A CLAIM IS A PROPOSITION ABOUT THE WORLD AND NAMES NO READER. The
boundary against the Leg's other fields is one of grammatical kind:
`purpose` is a verb about the reader and carries no proposition from
the material, and `rationale` is the order argument. A claim that
mentions the reader, or a purpose that could be true or false of the
world, is in the wrong field.
ONE CLAIM PER STRAND NAMED IN `materials`. Two claims in one Leg
naming the same Strand is REFUSED, naming the Leg and the Strand. A
Strand that serves several Legs carries a DIFFERENT claim in each --
that is what makes the path a sequence rather than a restatement, and it
is why the rule is per Leg rather than per path.
WHY THE CARDINALITY IS BOUNDED AT ALL, measured rather than argued
(kogaki#1108). The Leg Packet requires every declared claim to be
recoverable from the realized passage, and `claims` fails the
Leg otherwise. With cardinality unbounded, claim generation drifted
into composing the article's decisive lines wholesale and calling them
claims -- so the comparison the Packet performs stopped measuring
grounding and started measuring how much of the passage had been written
in advance. One proposition per Strand is what keeps a claim a claim
the Strand supports rather than a draft of the sentence that will carry
it.
A CLAIM IS ONE PROPOSITION DERIVED FROM A STRAND, AND NOTHING ELSE. The
type set is closed at `strand`. What the reader already holds is the
computed `already knows` ledger and the Persona's prior knowledge.
Neither is an
assertion, so a passage that realizes its Leg correctly never states
one and the Blind Reader never recovers it.
The claims rule is the spec half of this definition; the mechanical half -- the closed type set and the one-per-Strand refusal -- is carried here and enforced by `validateLegs`.

retired_types.leg_effect: inherited reader state, which is already carried by the computed `already knows` ledger
retired_types.reader_assumption: a presupposed premise, which belongs to the Persona's prior knowledge

type.description: The closed set above. Today it has one member, `strand`.

proposition.description: The claim itself, STATED -- a specific proposition this Leg asserts, not a pointer at where one could be found. An untyped pointer is not a claim.

strand.description: The Strand this claim is asserted on behalf of, as a LessonDisplayID (`L<n>`). It is where the pinned Lesson that grounds the claim is addressed, and no other claim of this Leg names it.

definition: A WAYPOINT IS A POINT ITS PARAGRAPH MAKES (kogaki#1326, owner decision
2026-10-10). The Leg's waypoints say, in order, what the Leg's paragraphs
establish.
A POINT, NEVER AN EFFECT AND NEVER A SENTENCE TO COPY. `point` is the
proposition the paragraph makes, in one sentence. It names what the
paragraph establishes -- never how the reader is to feel, what they are
"handed", or when they "receive" something. The point is not quoted: its
wording is the writer's.
IT CARRIES RELATIONS AND SERVES CLAIMS (kogaki#1768). In a Brief /brief
composed, `carries` names the relation or higher-order relation ids of the
Brief's `structure` the point states, and `serves` is derived from them: the
claims those relations are `from`. A Brief with no `structure` carries no
`carries`, and a waypoint carrying it there is refused.
NO MOVE INFORMATION REACHES THE BRIEF. The paragraph Move each waypoint is
planned with is bound AFTER the Brief, by the ParagraphPlan stage
(`/paragraph-plan`, kogaki#1375), which keeps which Move it bound in its run
directory.
IT RECORDS WHOSE CASE ITS PARAGRAPH TELLS (kogaki#1732, owner ruling
2026-11-07). `case` records whether its paragraph tells the proposition's own
case or a case apart, in material the reader already holds. The waypoint
after an `apart` one carries that structure onto the subject.
WHAT IS REFUSED IS SHAPE, AND THE COUNT IS NOT. `validateLegs` refuses an
empty list, a waypoint with an empty `point` or an empty `serves`, a waypoint
with no `case` or a `case` other than `own` and `apart`, a Leg whose last
waypoint is `apart`, a waypoint carrying the retired `effect`, `move` or
`segments`, a `serves` entry naming a Strand this Leg carries no claim for, a
claim of this Leg that no waypoint serves, and, in a Brief with a `structure`,
a waypoint carrying no `carries` or a `carries` id not in it -- each naming the
Leg and the waypoint. Whether a point is grounded in what it carries is
judged, by the GROUNDED judgment, and never a lint.

point.description: The proposition this paragraph makes, in the article's subject, in one sentence -- what the paragraph establishes. Never how the reader is to feel or what they are handed, and never a sentence for the writer to copy: its wording is the writer's.

serves.description: The claim or claims of this Leg this step serves, each named by the Strand id its claim names (`L<n>`). Every entry is a Strand this Leg carries a claim for.

carries.description: The relation or higher-order relation ids of the Brief's `structure` this point states (kogaki#1768). Required in a Brief that carries a `structure`, refused in one that carries none.

case.description: Whose case this paragraph tells. `own`: the proposition's own case, in the subject's domain. `apart`: a case apart from the proposition's domain, in material the reader already holds -- chosen from the Persona's prior knowledge and this Leg's claims. The waypoint after an `apart` one carries that case's structure onto the subject, so a Leg never ends on `apart`. It records what you decided when you wrote the waypoint; it adds no paragraph.

what_is_judged_elsewhere: Nothing here is a lint over a judgment. Whether a point is grounded in the
relations it carries is judged by the GROUNDED judgment at composition, and
whether a Section opens where the reader's question changes by the
`leg_sections` row; a refusal from this file always names a SHAPE.
Every MUST is judgment, and nothing becomes a lint -- which is the rule this paragraph is an instance of.
